chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ismail ibn Bashaar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him, so he said to him, 'May Allah keep you well! Is the drinking of wine more evil or the abandoning of the Prayer?' He said: 'The drinking of wine.' Then he said: 'Or do you know why that is so?' He said, 'No.' He said: 'Because he comes to be in a state in which he does not recognize his Lord with it.'
ai.seo_question: Why is drinking wine considered worse than missing prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the consumption of wine above the neglect of prayer by highlighting the loss of *ma'rifah* (divine awareness) inherent in intoxication. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that while missing prayer is a sin of omission, wine induces a state of spiritual blindness where one is effectively disconnected from God, making it the 'gateway' to all other sins.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ismail Bin Bashaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! Is the wine drinker more evil or the neglector of the Prayer?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wine drinker’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or do you know why that is so?’ He said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because he comes to be in such a state that he does not recognise in it, his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ’Isma‘il ibn Bashshar who has said the following:

“Once a man asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, is drinking wine more evil or not performing Salat (prayer)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Drinking wine is more evil.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Do you know why?’ The man said, ‘No, I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because he ends up in a condition in which he does not know his Lord.’”
